claim_under_test: U1: a batched (numpy) world raises env-ticks per second over the scalar reference at equal receipts
verdict: FALSIFIED for this world: 0.7x world-only at every batch size, 0.93-0.94x end to end on long-lived runs, 1.3-1.8x on short-lived runs (setup amortisation, not stepping). The vectorised transition was never the cost; the per-env contract (events, JSON trace text, pending queue) and the players are. Batching pays only when the CONTRACT is batchable (columnar events, array trace) and players/observers batch too -- that is a different world family under SEMANTIC/aggregate agreement, not BIT trace equality.
